nodes.description: HMFOR performance in 1 M KOH with 50 mM HMF
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic HMFOR performance was evaluated in 1 M KOH solution with 50 mM HMF, utilizing a typical three-electrode system. As shown in Fig. 3a, ... After the addition of HMF, the onset potential of HMFOR is about 1.37 V ... a current density of 1300 mA cm⁻² can be achieved at the potential of 1.5 V ... Until the transferred charge reaches 580 C, the conversion of HMF is close to 100%, with selectivity of FDCA and Faradic efficiency are both over 98%.

nodes.description: HMFOR performance in 1 M KOH with 50 mM HMF
nodes.source_text: Compared with Ni(OH)₂ and Cu(OH)₂, Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ exhibits extremely impressive performance of HMFOR, a current density of 1300 mA cm⁻² can be achieved at the potential of 1.5 V, which is 3.67 times than that of Ni(OH)₂ (354 mA cm⁻²)

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer HMFOR||HER with 100 mM HMF
nodes.source_text: a 2 cm × 2 cm anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer was assembled with Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ as anode and Ni foam as cathode for the continuous conversion of HMF at the concentration of 100 mM ... up to 1 A can be achieved at a low cell voltage of 1.7 V. Relying on this system, HMF can be converted consistently and stably at 1.65 V with an impressive one-way conversion rate of more than 85% ... Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ remains generally stable during up to 380 h of continuous conversion. After three cycles, the conversion of HMF was close to 100% and 11.12 g of FDCA could be obtained ... with a weight-based yield close to 88.3%

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images reveal in situ growth of Cu(OH)₂ nanowires with smooth surfaces on Cu foam, becoming rough after Ni²⁺ modification for Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images reveal the in situ growth of Cu(OH)₂ nanowires with smooth surfaces on the Cu foam after alkali etching (Fig. 1b-c). Followed by Ni²⁺ modification, the surface of the nanowires becomes rough (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show sharp metallic Cu diffraction peaks at 43.3°, 50.4° and 74.1°, characteristic peaks of Cu(OH)₂ (JCPDS No. 35-0505), but no obvious peaks for poorly crystallized Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns show sharp metallic Cu diffraction peaks at 43.3°, 50.4° and 74.1°, while characteristic peaks of Cu(OH)₂ (JCPDS No. 35-0505) can be observed after immersion (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show Cu(OH)₂ as inner core with Ni(OH)₂ shell layer, with interlayer spacing of ~0.232 nm (015) plane of Ni(OH)₂ and ~0.250 nm (111) plane of Cu(OH)₂ at the interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1e, Cu(OH)₂ as the inner core and the surface-covered Ni(OH)₂ shell layer can be clearly observed. The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ depict two interlayer spacing of ~0.232 nm and ~0.250 nm on both sides of the interface (Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mappings verify Cu mainly distributed in the inner core of nanowire while Ni uniformly dispersed in the shell layer of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Corresponding element mappings (EDS) of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ further verify that Cu is mainly distributed in the inner core of the nanowire while Ni is uniformly dispersed in the shell layer (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work functions of Ni(OH)₂ (5.03 eV) and Cu(OH)₂ (4.57 eV), with Δφ of 0.46 eV at interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the calculated φ of Ni(OH)₂ and Cu(OH)₂ are 5.03 eV and 4.57 eV, respectively, exhibiting a relatively large Δφ of 0.46 eV at Ni(OH)₂-Cu(OH)₂ interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS shows peaks at 855.9 eV and 873.9 eV for Ni²⁺ at surface; after Ar⁺ sputtering, Niδ⁺ (δ<2) peaks appear and Cu²⁺ signal increases, indicating lower valent Ni at interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ shows two main peaks of 855.9 eV and 873.9 eV could be assigned to Ni²⁺ at the surface of Ni(OH)₂ (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized XANES shows Cu K-edge slight shift to higher energy vs Cu(OH)₂ and Ni K-edge to lower energy vs Ni(OH)₂, verifying electron transfer at interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the Cu K-edge of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ shows slight shift towards higher energy compared with Cu(OH)₂ while Ni K-edge towards lower energy compared with Ni(OH)₂ (Fig. 2c-d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra show local coordination structures of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ similar to Ni(OH)₂ and Cu(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transformed (FT) - extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra in R-space exhibits the local coordination structures of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ are similar to Ni(OH)₂ and Cu(OH)₂ (Fig. S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region at different scan rates gives Cdl = 7.64 mF cm⁻² for Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ (vs 2.41 mF cm⁻² Ni(OH)₂, 3.79 mF cm⁻² Cu(OH)₂), indicating greatly enhanced ECSA from hierarchical multilayer assembly.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Obtained by CV curves at different scan rates in non-Faradic interval (Fig. S5), the calculated Cdl value of Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ is 7.64 mFcm⁻², much higher than Ni(OH)₂ (2.41 cm⁻²) and Cu(OH)₂ (3.79 mF cm⁻²) (Fig. 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of interfacial water shows peaks at 3600 cm⁻¹ (isolated K⁺ water), 3450 cm⁻¹ (2-HB H₂O), 3200 cm⁻¹ (4-HB H₂O); Ni(OH)₂/Cu(OH)₂ has higher weak/strong H-bond ratio indicating attenuated H-bond network.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4a-c, three different peaks represent the stretching vibration model of U-OH of water, which corresponding to K⁺ water (isolated water, 3600 cm⁻¹), 2-coordinated hydrogen-bonded water (2-HB·H₂O, 3450 cm⁻¹) and 4-coordinated hydrogen-bonded water (4-HB·H₂O, 3200 cm⁻¹).
